newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Learjet wreckage may have been found - SIA.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Learjet wreckage may have been found - SIA.

text.p: Thai searchers have found the wreckage of a plane believed to be the Singapore Learjet which disappeared four days ago with two people aboard, Singapore Airlines (SIA) said on Thursday.
"The Thai authorities have found the wreckage of an aircraft and in their view it is the SIA Learjet," airline spokesman Karmjit Singh said in a statement. "We are waiting for verification."
Singh said the wreckage was spotted on a remote mountain ridge after an intense search in southern Thailand which was hampered by bad weather.
The search began with hours of the Learjet disappearing from radar screens on Monday afternoon.
An Australian pilot and a Singaporean trainee were aboard the Learjet 31 training aircraft when it left the Thai resort island of Phuket for Ranong, 170 km (106 miles) farther north.
SIA has declined to name the 54-year-old Australian and the 28-year-old Singaporean at the request of their families.
